relevance_note: Retrospective Mayo Clinic series describing 13 individually tabulated patients with late-onset Alexander disease: "Thirteen patients with type II AxD were identified."; one GFAP variant is printed for patient 10.
method_note: Patients 1-13 are table columns in Table 1 (header 'characteristics of patients with Alexander disease - Patient - k') and Table 2 (header 'Patient - 1', '2', ... '13'); labels follow the text's 'Patient N'. A short Python script in the scratch directory sliced the table-row spans (row label through the patient's cell) and read sex, ages and presenting symptom from Table 1 and the graded cells (Mild/Mod/Severe) from Table 2; the output was checked against the tables by eye. Most cells of Table 1 (Nystagmus ... Psychiatric symptom) and many of Table 2 hold only the symbols '1' and '2' (apparently converted from +/- signs), and the paper's legend and text never define them; under the table-symbol rule these cells were recorded as not reported, both for observed and excluded. Text and figure legends that name a patient were used instead (e.g. patient 3's absent palatal tremor and nystagmus, patient 2's hyperreflexia/Babinski/weakness, which agree with the coded cells). The slash-coded cells (brainstem enhancement and pial FLAIR, 'midbrain/pons/medulla') are per-region codes of the same undefined kind, not recorded; 'Not obtained' and 'No contrast' cells are not reported. Patients 6 and 9 were identified as 'the 2 youngest patients (age at onset 12 and 13 years)' from Table 1 onset ages; the statement 'They were the only 2 patients with a periventricular rim' was used to exclude the rim for the other 11 (inferred from group statement). 'In our series, palatal tremor was present in only one patient' does not name the patient, so it was not assigned. The third thalamic/basal ganglia patient is not named in text, so only patients 2 and 4 (Figure 3 legend) are observed. Group counts (e.g. 'Eleven of 12 had pial FLAIR signal change', 'Ten subjects had a positive family history') were not assigned to individuals. Genotypes: 'Eight patients had mutations in the GFAP gene (see table e-1)'; table e-1 is an unavailable supplement, so the eight are not identifiable and get no variant rows. Only patient 10 has a printed variant ('c.1154C.G ... p.Ser385Cys', recorded as printed; the '.' is likely a converted '>'). Patient 3 is not stated to carry it (only the father's analysis confirmed patient 3's diagnosis), so no variant row for patient 3. Relatives: Patient 13 is the mother of patient 12, patient 10 the father of patient 3, patient 8 the son of patient 2; Patient 4's daughter (autopsy consistent with AxD) is an additional in-scope relative, recorded as deceased because she had an autopsy. Patient 3's 'essentially normal neurologic examination at presentation' is a whole-examination statement and was not turned into specific exclusions. Presenting symptoms that do not clearly match a checklist item (weakness without limb, memory complaint, gait difficulty, vocal cord dysfunction, nausea) left the checklist item not reported; urinary frequency and bladder incontinence were taken as bladder dysfunction. No internal contradictions found; patient 2's text ages (presented at 65 with 2 years of weakness) agree with Table 1 (onset 63, diagnosis 65).
